Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's segmentation adapters learn transferable localisation from image-level labels alone? Today they learn only from pixel masks of BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC. We replace the Dice and Focal seg_loss with a multiple-instance objective applied at all four levels to the segmentation-branch patch-to-text similarity map (mean of the top 2% patch anomaly probabilities; max and mean pooling as ablations), and train on all five source datasets with masks discarded. Primary question and hypothesis: because every patch is scored against a shared text anchor, image-level supervision aligns patch-level evidence with the text 'abnormal' direction, so the learned localisation transfers to the unseen modality and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-level AUROC (with PRO and image AUROC also reported). A visual-only MIL control (same operator on a linear patch classifier without text anchors) tests whether text anchoring is responsible. Secondary analyses: per-level localisation quality, and a label-budget comparison on two held-out modalities between image-labelled training and mask-supervised training on 10%, 30% and 100% of the masked images.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: DINO-affinity propagation of MIL evidence into pseudo-masks
SUMMARY: Train with image-level MIL first, then refine the resulting patch maps of abnormal source images by random-walk propagation over a frozen DINOv2 patch-affinity graph into pseudo-masks that supervise MVFA's segmentation adapters.
HYPOTHESIS: DINO-affinity-refined pseudo-masks improve held-out PRO by at least 3 points over unrefined MIL maps, and the resulting segmentation branch retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-AUROC margin over chance.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: pseudo-mask refinement (none vs. DINO affinity propagation vs. CLIP-feature affinity). Stage 1: top-k MIL on the seg branch (image labels only). Stage 2: for each abnormal training image, compute DINOv2 ViT-S/14 patch features at 238x238 (17x17 patches, matching MVFA's grid), affinity A_ij = max(0, cos)^beta (beta = 8), row-normalise, propagate the stage-1 map m: m' = (alpha A + (1 - alpha) I)^t m with alpha = 0.7, t = 3; pseudo-mask = m' > 0.5 x max(m'). Stage 3: train seg adapters with Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask IoU against true masks (analysis only), pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities.
RATIONALE: Image-level MIL localises only the few most anomalous patches and produces fragmented maps. DINO features are spatially coherent and cluster anatomically consistent regions, so affinity propagation over DINO patch similarities can grow MIL seeds into region-shaped pseudo-masks, giving the segmentation branch dense, shape-aware supervision without any expert mask.
METHOD: 1) Stage 1 as top-k MIL on seg tokens (loss.py: topk_mil). 2) New script refine_masks.py: torch.hub DINOv2 ViT-S/14 (frozen, about 22M parameters), resize to 238, patch features 17x17x384, affinity and propagation in numpy; save pseudo-masks. 3) Stage 3: existing Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks for all source images (normal: empty). 4) DINO is used only offline on source training images, not at test time, so inference cost is unchanged. 5) Hyper-parameters: alpha, beta, t as above (ablations alpha in {0.5, 0.7, 0.9}, t in {1, 3, 5}).
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); masks of the source datasets are discarded for all image-label-supervised variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities using image AUROC only (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds; evaluation on the held-out modalities that have masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) for pixel metrics and on all six for image AUROC. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; MIL only; CLIP-affinity propagation (same procedure with CLIP layer-24 features). Ablations: propagation parameters; DINOv2 ViT-S vs. ViT-B. Metrics: pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC; pseudo-mask IoU (analysis). Falsification: no PRO gain over MIL-only.

Idea B:
TITLE: Counterfactual patch replacement: learning where anomalies are from which patches, when replaced by normal tissue, flip the image decision
SUMMARY: For each abnormal source image, replace each patch's adapted feature by its nearest neighbour from that dataset's normal-patch bank and measure the drop in the image-level anomaly score; patches with the largest counterfactual drop become pseudo-masks for the segmentation adapters.
HYPOTHESIS: Counterfactual-drop pseudo-masks achieve higher pixel IoU with true masks than top-k MIL maps on BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC training images (by at least 0.1), and segmentation adapters trained on them retain at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's held-out pixel-AUROC margin over chance.
RATIONALE: By analogy with counterfactual explanations and inpainting-based anomaly localisation, an anomalous region is the part of an image whose replacement by normal content makes the image normal. Image labels suffice to define both sides: the image-level detector (trained on labels) and the normal content (patches of labelled normal images of the same dataset). Unlike MIL, which only selects the top-scoring patches, the counterfactual test measures causal contribution to the decision, which should be less sensitive to spurious high scores.
METHOD: 1) Train MVFA's detection branch with image labels (unchanged). 2) For each source dataset, build a coreset bank (10%) of adapted normal patch tokens per level. 3) For each abnormal image and each patch j, replace token j at all levels by its nearest bank token, recompute the image score (mean-pooled softmax as in train_zero.py), drop_j = s - s_(j). Batch all 289 replacements in one forward pass of the scoring head (no backbone re-run needed because only post-adapter tokens are replaced). 4) Pseudo-mask: patches with drop above the 95th percentile, foreground-restricted. 5) Train segmentation adapters with Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks. 6) Code: make_counterfactual_masks.py, train_zero.py loss swap.
EXPERIMENT: BMAD zero-shot leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); no source masks used by the proposed variants; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation splits by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as reference; 3 seeds; pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; top-k MIL; normal-bank kNN pseudo-masks. Ablations: replacement at one level vs all levels; percentile; group replacement of 2x2 patch windows. Metrics: pseudo-mask IoU (analysis), held-out pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC. Falsification: IoU gain below 0.05 over MIL maps.
